comments.content: The 3-4KB baseline assumes a static cardinality problem, but you're right that churn rate is the hidden multiplier most teams miss—if those million series from the user_id label turn over frequently, you're not just holding 3GB in memory, you're constantly allocating and discarding blocks. Have you found that teams typically discover this through production memory spikes, or do some catch it during load testing with realistic label distributions?
